rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction is an instance of ellipsis by reciprocal omission, or something close to it, illustrated by the cited battle verse.
rows.anchor: فهو احتباك أو قريب منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prevails over every intended outcome: each effort to suppress Joseph's name, kill or sell him, or accuse him instead becomes a means to his elevation and vindication.
rows.anchor: { والله } أي الملك الأعظم { غالب على أمره } أي الأمر الذي يريده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people fail to perceive God's mastery because they attend to visible causes and appearances, which veil him from them.
rows.anchor: { لا يعلمون } لعدم التأمل أنه تعالى عال على كل أمر

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah account says Joseph was seventeen, Jacob favored him and gave him a special tunic, and his dreams intensified his brothers' hatred; they later plotted against him, Reuben diverted them to a dry pit, Judah arranged his sale for twenty pieces, and the brothers bloodied his tunic to deceive Jacob, who mourned him. Al-Biqāʿī says parts conflict with the Qur'an's apparent account but may be interpreted.
rows.anchor: ذكر ما مضى من قصة يوسف عليه الصلاة والسلام من التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report of Joseph's adulthood follows God's statement of his intended provision, showing that the divine act is realized and demonstrating complete power and knowledge.
rows.anchor: أتبعه الإعلام بإيجاد ذلك الفعل دلالة على تمام القدرة وشمول العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashudd means Joseph's powers had come together and reached maturity.
rows.anchor: { ولما بلغ أشده } أي مجتمع قواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gives two readings of ḥukm: prophethood, or a faculty that restrains desire so that speech and action follow sound judgment; al-Rummānī defines judgment as distinguishing what evidence establishes.
rows.anchor: { حكما } أي نبوة أو ملكة يكف بها النفس عن هواها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge means clarifying a thing as it is, and was granted as recompense for Joseph's excellence.
rows.anchor: { وعلما } أي تبيينا للشيء على ما هو عليه جزاء له لأنه محسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rewards all who excel in goodness, with Muhammad foremost among them, raised by the Night Journey above others.
rows.anchor: الذين رأسهم محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم الذي أسرى به

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Whoever worships God well in youth is given wisdom in middle age.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : من أحسن عبادة الله في شبيبته آتاه الله الحكمة في اكتهاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashudd denotes full strength; Sibawayh treats it as a plural of shiddah, while another view derives it from shadd.
rows.anchor: والأشد : كمال القوة , وهو جمع شدة عند سيبوبه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One report sets the age of ashudd at twenty; another says it begins at puberty, and the author notes further reports without specifying them.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه من عشرين سنة

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Al-Mujmal records disagreement over whether ashudd has a singular: some say it has none, while others give shadd; the author notes analogous plural patterns.
rows.anchor: قال ابن فارس في المجمل : وبعضهم يقول : لا واحد لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāwadat means she repeatedly addressed and maneuvered Joseph through stratagems; her being his householder and his youth made her access to him especially complete, while “about himself” indicates that he alone was her object.
rows.anchor: { وراودته } أي راجعته الخطاب ودارت عليه بالحيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven permutations of the weak root r-w-d revolve around circling back, yielding senses such as seeking, coming and going, gentleness, deliberation, maneuver, and good judgment.
rows.anchor: مادة ( راد ) واوية ويائية بجميع تقاليبها السبعة : رود , ودور , وورد

rows.speaker: ابن دريد
rows.claim: Ibn Duraid says the root's scout means one seeking a need; the author connects this with searching over ground without a fixed destination.
rows.anchor: وكل طالب حاجة - قاله ابن دريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other derivatives preserve the same turning or movement image: a kohl applicator turns in the eye, a waterside arrival is called wurūd, and a wavering cushion does not settle; the extensive examples explain the maneuvering sense of rāwadat.
rows.anchor: والمرود : الذي يكتحل به , لأنه يدار في العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensive form ghallaqat conveys that she shut the doors repeatedly or firmly to increase her control; it is said there were seven, and closure means fastening a door so it is hard to open.
rows.anchor: { وغلقت } أي تغليفا كثيرا { الأبواب } زيادة في المكنة , قالوا : وكانت سبعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase hayta laka means she prepared herself for him alone and called him to come and obey; the word is read with several vowelings and can mean “come.”
rows.anchor: { وقالت هيت } أي تهيأت وتصنعت { لك } خاصة فأقبل إلي وامتثل أمري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He invokes God's protection from the proposed deed.
rows.anchor: { معاذ } أي أعوذ من هذا الأمر معاذ { الله } أي ألزم حصن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's “my Lord” refers to God, his creator and benefactor, rather than the husband; this reading makes his appeal an act of piety and also entails loyalty to the man who trusted him, whereas the husband-only reading would not entail God-consciousness.
rows.anchor: وهذا التقدير - مع كونه أليق بالصالحين المراقبين - أحسن , لأنه يستلزم نصح العزيز , ولو أعدنا الضمير على العزيز لم يستلزم التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the master gave Joseph a place of honor and entrusted his possessions to him, yielding would betray both God and the trust placed in him.
rows.anchor: بأن جعل لي في قلب سيدك مكانة عظيمة حتى خولني في جميع ما يملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongdoers do not prosper: if Joseph yielded, he would join those who put things in the wrong place and would not attain success.
rows.anchor: { أنه لا يفلح } أي لا يظفر بمراده أصلا { الظالمون } أي العريقون في الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's response shows his judgment and knowledge: at a dangerous moment he sought refuge in God, recalled the beneficence that required gratitude, and considered the grief and failure injustice brings.
rows.anchor: فإنه لما رأى المقام الدحض بادر إلى الاعتصام بمن بيده ملكوت كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The woman firmly intended intercourse, while Joseph would have intended it had he not seen his Lord's proof; because that proof was present to his inward sight, desire did not cover it and he did not intend the act at all.
rows.anchor: { ولقد همت به } أي أوقعت الهم , وهو القصد الثابت والعزم الصادق المتعلق بمواقعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without the proof Joseph had the strength and youthful readiness to be tempted, but the light of witnessing God erased the intention; his purity, later preference for prison, and being among the sincere support this interpretation.
rows.anchor: فلم يهم أصلا مع كونه في غاية الاستعداد لذلك لما آتاه الله من القوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a conditional lولا construction, the omitted result must continue the meaning already supplied by the preceding clause: here Joseph would have intended her, just as the daughter of Pharaoh would have disclosed Moses in 28:10 had God not steadied her heart.
rows.anchor: إن كادت لتبدي به لولا أن ربطنا على قلبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports from early authorities that imply Joseph actually intended sin are not soundly transmitted, contradict one another when combined, and lack support in Arabic syntax; al-Rāzī calls the author's reading the position of the verified commentators, and Abū Ḥayyān also points it out.
rows.anchor: نبه على ذلك الإمام أبو حيان , وسبقه إلى ذلك الإمام الرازي وقال : إن هذا قول المحققين من المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both raced with utmost effort: Joseph fled her, while she tried to stop him; he reached the farthest door first, but its locks forced him to work at opening it, allowing her to seize his shirt.
rows.anchor: { واستبقا الباب } أي أوجد المسابقة بغاية الرغبة من كل منهما , هذا للهرب منها , وهذه لمنعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb takes “the door” directly without the preposition “to,” signaling that both exerted their full effort to win the race.
rows.anchor: فأوصل الفعل إلى المفعول بدون ( إلى ) , دليلا على أن كلا منهما بذل أقصى جهده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She caught the nearest part of his garment from behind and tore away a piece, which remained in her hand.
rows.anchor: وكان القد { من دبر } أي الناحية منه , وانقطعت منه قطعة فبقيت في يدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular “her master” is used because Joseph had never entered slavery and a Muslim cannot be owned; the pair appeared disheveled when they found him at the outer door.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل : سيدهما , لأن يوسف عليه الصلاة والسلام لم يدخل في رق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The woman's “what is the recompense?” may be read as a denial or as a question; she proposes imprisonment for an indefinite time or some other lasting painful punishment for anyone accused of seeking evil with her household.
rows.anchor: { ما } نافية , ويجوز أن تكون استفهامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Caught unexpectedly, she spoke at once and without shame; Joseph initially followed noble restraint, staying silent to shield her and avoid naming the indecency.
rows.anchor: وأما هو عليه الصلاة والسلام فجرى على سجايا الكرام بأن سكت سترا عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph defended himself only after she accused him of betrayal, and used the third-person “she” out of modesty rather than addressing her directly.
rows.anchor: ولما كان كل صالح للشهادة كافيا , فلم تدع ضرورة إلى تعيينه

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: The witness was an infant from her family; al-Rummānī transmits this from Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Hurayra, and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and compares it with a newborn boy from Yamāma who testified to the Prophet's messengership and was called Mubārak al-Yamāma.
rows.anchor: رضيع براءته - نقله الرماني عن ابن عباس وأبي هريرة رضي الله عنهما وسعيد ابن جبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condition requires an understood act of discernment, since conditional meanings are future even when their verbs are past; a tear in front would support her account, though it would not by itself prove Joseph lied unless he had pursued her.
rows.anchor: ولا بد من تقدير فعل التبين , لأن الشروط لا تكون معانيها إلا مستقبلة ولو كانت ألفاظها ماضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A back tear shows she lied and Joseph spoke truth, since it follows from his turning away and her pursuit; the passive form of “torn” leaves the agent disputed.
rows.anchor: لأنه لولا إدباره عنها وإقبالها عليه لما وقع ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here in means an inference that establishes one outcome from another, not doubt; the speaker presents her evidence first to appear to favor her husband, while actually proving her lie by implication and explicitly.
rows.anchor: وقدم أمارة صدقها لأنه مما يحبه سيدها , فهو في الظاهر اهتمام بها , وفي الحقيقة تقرير لكذبها مرتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The husband confirms her plot after seeing the back tear; he calls women's plotting great because it is subtler and more concealed than men's, though it is weak against God's power to undo it.
rows.anchor: معشر النساء ؛ والكيد : طلب الإنسان بما يكرهه { إن كيدكن عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains the plot's subtlety by saying Satan has greater access to women because of their deficiency, while their plotting remains feeble beside God's power to cancel it.
rows.anchor: لأن الشيطان عليهن لنقصهن أقدر , وكيدهن الذي هو من كيد الشيطان أضعف ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The husband tells Joseph to turn wholly away from the incident and not discuss it, since his innocence is clear, then tells her to seek forgiveness so neither he nor God punishes her; the verb for sin implies deliberate wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: { واستغفري } أي اطلبي الغفران { لذنبك } في أن لا يحصل لك عقوبة مني ولا من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women gossip as a group in the city; they attach the wife to her high-status husband to spread the news, since people attend to stories about the eminent, and the term ʿazīz means invulnerable through power.
rows.anchor: فأضفتها إلى زوجها إرادة الإشاعة للخبر ، لأن النفس إلى سماع أخبار أولي الأخطار أميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense rāwid conveys her persistence as seduction has become habitual; “her youth” can lower her status to desiring her own slave.
rows.anchor: وعبرن بالمضارع في { تراود فتاها } أي عبدها نازلة من افتراش العزيز إلأى افتراشه { عن نفسه } إفهاما لأن الإصرار على المراودة صار لها كالسجية

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī restricts fatā to a strong young man, whereas al-Zajjāj says a slave was called fatā whether young or old.
rows.anchor: والفتى : الشاب ، وقيده الرماني بالقوي

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: People called a male slave fatā regardless of whether he was old or young.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : وكانوا يسمون المملوك فتى شيخا كان أو شابا

rows.speaker: السدي وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: They explain shighāf as the heart's covering, a skin over it through which love reaches the heart.
rows.anchor: دخل الحب الجلد حتى أصاب القلب ، عن السدى وأبي عبيدة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes shighāf to mean the inner part of the heart.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن أنه باطن القلب

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī takes shighāf to mean the middle of the heart.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي علي : وسط القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mujmal and other lexicons also define shighāf as the heart's covering.
rows.anchor: والذي قال في المجمل وغيره أنه غلاف القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers understanding the love itself as having become her enclosing heart-veil, a better explanation than Abū ʿUbayda's account.
rows.anchor: وأحسن من توجيه أبي عبيدة له أن حبه صار شغافا لها ، أي حجابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant with the undotted letter means that love covered the heart's shighāf, the core near the attachment of its tendon; al-Rummānī also glosses the expression as taking her wholly over, like the peaks of mountains.
rows.anchor: وأما شغفها - بالمهملة فمعناه : غشى شغفه قلبها ، وهي رأسه عند معلق النياط

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī also explains the phrase as love taking her in every direction, by comparison with mountain summits called shighāf.
rows.anchor: وقال الرماني : أي ذهب بها كل مذهب ، من شغف الجبال ، وهي رؤوسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who saw Joseph excused her and concluded that they too would have acted as she did in her place.
rows.anchor: لأن من رآه عذرها وقطع بأنهن لو كن يفي محلها عملن عملها ولم يظللن فعلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph explains that he left a people who disbelieve in God and the afterlife; despite their power to harm and imprison him after signs of his truth, such conduct shows they do not consider consequences.
rows.anchor: نبه على أن ذلك لا يقدم عليه إلا من لا يحسب العاقبة بوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated pronoun in “they are disbelievers in the afterlife” marks their distinctive ignorance: denying the afterlife darkens their hearts and makes them mere forms without understanding.
rows.anchor: وفي تكرير الضمير تنبيه على أن هؤلاء اختصوا بهذا الجهل

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī defines milla as a community's shared religious way that protects its members, deriving the term from a fever embedded in a person.
rows.anchor: والملة : مذهب جماعة يحمي بعضها لبعض في الديانة

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qāmūs explains malīla as heat lodged in the bone.
rows.anchor: وفي القاموس إن المليلة : الحر الكامن في العظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph says “I left” rather than “I avoided” a religion he had never practiced, as a conciliatory way to draw the prisoners toward abandoning it.
rows.anchor: مع كونه لم يلابس تلك الملة قط , تأنيسا لهما واستدراجا إلى تركهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph invokes his prophetic lineage to persuade the prisoners: Abraham is his ancestor, Isaac his grandfather, and Jacob his father; the ḥanīf way follows evidence rather than desire or rigid attachment.
rows.anchor: بأنه من بيت النبوة ومعدن الفتوة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In a report in al-Bukhārī's Tafsīr, the Prophet says the most honored person is the most God-fearing; when asked specifically about lineage, he names Joseph son of Jacob son of Isaac son of Abraham, then says the best in the pre-Islamic era are best in Islam when they understand religion.
rows.anchor: روى البخاري في التفسير وغيره عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's household could not associate anything with God, since knowledge of the sound religion left no ambiguity and ruled out every kind of creature as a partner.
rows.anchor: لما عندنا من نور العلم الذي لم يدع عندنا لبسا بوجه أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Monotheism is a divine favor to Joseph's family and humanity: God made the original disposition receptive to it, and gratitude for every unowed divine gift is obligatory by reason and revelation.
rows.anchor: والفضل : النفع الزائد على مقدار الواجب , فكل عطاء الله فضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses reciprocal ellipsis: denying association first implies that others do associate, while saying later that most do not give thanks implies that Joseph and some people do.
rows.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : ذكر نفي الشرك أولا يدل على وجوده ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After demonstrating his prophethood through foreknowledge and inviting the prisoners to Islam, Joseph follows transmitted proofs with the rational argument of mutual prevention against every religion other than the prophets' shared monotheism.
rows.anchor: أتبعه برهان التمانع على فساد كل ملة غير الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them “companions of prison” establishes intimate fellowship in a place of trial where counsel is sincere, hearts are purified, and both seek deliverance.
rows.anchor: فقال مناديا لهما باسم الصحبة بالأداة التي تقال عند ما له وقع عظيم في النفوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Distinct alleged gods would need places and are seen as inert; if alive, they could conflict, making each possibly powerless and therefore unfit for divinity.
rows.anchor: { أرباب } أي آلهة { متفرقون } متباينون بالذوات والحقائق تشاهدونه محتاجين إلى المكان مع كونهم جمادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question “which is better?” means which is greater in praise and more worthy of obedience; the rhetorical question invites the prisoners to return the answer themselves and softens the invitation.
rows.anchor: وأبرزه صلى الله عليه وسلم على وحه الاستفهام استجلابا للسامع برد العلم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph calls the idols “lords” and uses a comparative because this accepts the prisoners' own terms and makes the argument gentler and more likely to persuade.
rows.anchor: وسماها أربابا لمثل ذلك بناء على زعمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objects worshipped besides God are only names people and their ancestors invented; they have no souls, or, if alive, still lack the perfection of knowledge and power required for divinity.
rows.anchor: ما تعبدون من دونه إلا أسماء سميتموها أنتم وآباؤكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No revelation grants authority to honor these objects; the absence of divine warrant is decisive in this context, which does not require prolonged disputation.
rows.anchor: ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument concludes that authority belongs only to the one God: possible rivalry would entail possible impotence, while lifeless idols are even less worthy; God did not decree their worship.
rows.anchor: فعلم قطعا أنه لا حكم لمقهور , وأن كل من يمكن أن يكون له ثان مقهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to worship only God confirms that his judgment is binding; this is the straight religion, while most people fail to know because they follow appetites and do not use their minds.
rows.anchor: ذلك الدين القيم ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words are Joseph's, as their wisdom exceeds anyone else's knowledge in that age; the messenger had reported the women's testimony to his innocence, but Joseph puts vindication before the king's summons.
rows.anchor: والذي دل على أن ذلك كلامه ما فيه من الحكم التي لا يعرفها في ذلك الزمان غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” refers to Joseph's insistence on remaining imprisoned until the truth was clear, so the husband would know Joseph had not betrayed him while absent; the wife's confession in comfort and Joseph's steadfastness under hardship disclosed what was hidden.
rows.anchor: أي الخلق العظيم في تثبتي في السجن إلى أن تبين الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not guide the plots of habitual traitors to success; he exposes their betrayal, while Joseph's innocence is vindicated and his affairs directed toward good.
rows.anchor: بل لا بد أن يقيم سببا لظهور الخيانة وإن اجتهد الخائن في التعمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khiyāna is violating a general covenant, whereas ghadr is breaking a specific covenant.
rows.anchor: والخيانة : مخالفة الحق بنقض العهد العام . وضدها الأمانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph does not absolve himself of every slip or seek self-praise through his vindication; the self naturally commands evil intensely.
rows.anchor: عن مطلق الزلل وإن غلبه التوفيق والعصمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He offers three readings of “except those on whom my Lord has mercy”: God may restrain a soul from prompting evil, keep it from acting after prompting, or exempt souls whom mercy prevents from prompting evil.
rows.anchor: أو إلا ما رحمة ربي من النفوس فلا يأمر بسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's being forgiving and merciful answers anyone who might think repentance is unavailable.
rows.anchor: مؤكدا دفعا لظن من يظن أنه لا توبة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king is named again to avoid ambiguity after Joseph's intervening speech; “bring him to me” means the king seeks Joseph's exclusive service, forestalling the ʿAzīz's claim and any return to the wife's harassment.
rows.anchor: صرح به ولم يستغن بضميره كراهية الإلباس لما تخلل بينه وبين جواب امرأة العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author recounts that Joseph prayed for the prisoners, then bathed, cleaned himself, changed into new clothes, and hurried to the king; an inscription described prison as abodes of trial, graves of the living, houses of grief, and tests of friends and gloating enemies.
rows.anchor: وأجاب أمر الملك فأتى إليه بعد أن دعا لأهل السجن فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the king spoke seventy languages; Joseph understood them all, then addressed him in the language of his ancestors, which the king did not know, increasing the king's esteem for him.
rows.anchor: أنه قيل : إن الملك كان يتكلم بسبعين لسانا فكلمه بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makkīn means firmly established in a position from which one can attain one's aims, and amīn describes one trusted not to break an agreement.
rows.anchor: { لدينا مكين } أي شديد المكنة , من المكانة , وهي حالة يتمكن بها صاحبها من مراده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks to manage Egypt's storehouses so he can safeguard and administer provisions for people's welfare, and says he is capable of preserving what is entrusted and knowledgeable about managing and increasing it.
rows.anchor: { اجعلني } قيما { على خزائن الأرض } أي أرض مصر التي هي لكثرة خيرها كأنها الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His disclosure of both safeguarding ability and knowledge explains why he is suited to the task; it enables people to survive coming hardship and may draw them from false religion to truth.
rows.anchor: فأخبر بما جمع الله له من أداتي الحفظ والفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God enabled Joseph by giving him the king's affection and people's confidence, then authority over Egypt and the ability to settle wherever he wished, placing the kingdom and its surroundings under his hand.
rows.anchor: مثل ما مكنا ليوسف في قلب الملك من المودة والاعتقاد الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's enabling has two grounds: he grants mercy by his own choice, and he never wastes the reward of those who excel in worship, even though he could act otherwise.
rows.anchor: والثاني أنه محسن يعبد الله فانيا عن جميع الأغيار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Through al-Kalbī, Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Joseph was thirty when summoned; the king wondered that a young man interpreted his dream better than soothsayers, questioned him, then honored him.
rows.anchor: من طريق الكلبي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال : فأتاه الرسول

rows.speaker: عثمان بن صالح
rows.claim: ʿUthmān ibn Ṣāliḥ and others say the king was impressed as he questioned Joseph, gave him his signet, and entrusted him with authority beyond the palace gate; Ibn ʿAbbās's account adds that drums announced Joseph as the king's deputy in Egypt.
rows.anchor: قال عثمان - يعني ابن صالح - وغيره في حديثهما : فلما استنطقه وسايله

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima reports Pharaoh telling Joseph he had granted him Egypt but wanted his own throne four fingers taller; Joseph agreed.
rows.anchor: وعن عكرمة أن فرعون قال ليوسف : قد سلطتك على مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly power is not truly important unless joined to the bliss of the afterlife, whose reward is better; the verse stresses this against those who deny it.
rows.anchor: ولما كان هذ مما يستعظمه الناس في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife's better reward belongs to people marked by belief and persistent fear of God; describing them by these qualities is more persuasive than giving an unqualified command, and they have the highest rank.
rows.anchor: للذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account omits Joseph's actual administration of the storehouses because later events with his brothers are the story's central aim, though the verse's implications show that his management brought good and removed harm.
rows.anchor: وإنما طوى هذا للدلالة عليه بلوازمه من قصة إخوته التي هي المقصودة بالذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story exposes Egypt's dominant vice as hating foreigners, exploiting the weak, and submitting to the powerful: Egypt jailed Joseph despite his proven innocence, while he forgave its people, saved and freed them, and restored their wealth.
rows.anchor: الغالب على طبع مصر الرداءة : بغض الغريب , واستذلال الضعيف , والخضوع للقوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same national disposition later led Egyptians to enslave Israel's descendants and mistreat them despite Moses' rescue, signs, and scripture; their repeated disobedience led to the wilderness punishment until a later generation entered the promised lands.
rows.anchor: كانوا كل قليل ينكثون مجترئين على ما لا يطاق الاجتراء عليه

rows.speaker: داود
rows.claim: Al-Biqāʿī cites David's Psalm describing Israel's wilderness rebellion: the people are warned not to harden their hearts, after their ancestors tested God for forty years despite seeing his works.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر ذلك في زبور داود عليه الصلاة والسلام في غير موضع

rows.speaker: داود
rows.claim: The continuation of the cited Psalm recounts Israel's repeated rebellions: worshiping Baal Peor and a calf, rejecting the promised land and God's commands, sacrificing children, and being handed over to enemies after Moses and Phinehas interceded.
rows.anchor: صنعوا عجلا في حوريب , وسجدوا للمنحوت , وبدلوا مجدهم بشبه عجل يأكل عشبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Biqāʿī takes the Psalm's history as further evidence that God ultimately elevates the foreigner whom people had oppressed, as with Joseph and the Israelites.
rows.anchor: كما فعل بيوسف عليه الصلاة والسلام بعد السجن وببني إسرائيل بعد الاستعباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Residents of Egypt should guard against absorbing its supposed bad traits: lack of protective honor, hostility to foreigners, brazenness in falsehood, cowardice in truth, servility to tyrants, and evasive speech; they should keep examining themselves against God's commands, obey the Messenger, and love his example and that of his followers until it becomes their nature.
rows.anchor: فليحذر الساكن بها من أن يغلب عليه طبعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks God for protection from the self's evil, a good end, and inclusion among those who have no fear.
rows.anchor: أعاذنا الله من شرور أنفسنا وسيئات أعمالنا

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah account says Pharaoh dreamed twice two years later: seven healthy cows and full grain heads were followed by seven lean cows that swallowed them and seven thin heads that consumed the full ones; his magicians and sages could not interpret the dreams, so his cupbearer recalled Joseph's earlier prison interpretations and Pharaoh summoned him.
rows.anchor: ذكر ما مضى بعدما تقدم من هذه القصة من التوراة
